18:7584-1975

Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR REFERENCE FOOD COLOIJR BOXES

o.

FOR E \'\' 0

l~

D

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 25 February 1973, after the draft finalized by the Food Additives Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council, 0.2 IS: 6120-1971 * specifics a method of identification of constituent dyes and t wo methods for quantitative estimation of total dye content. For this purpose, the methods given in IS: 6120-1971* necessitate the use of standard food colours. Therefore, with a view to making available such standard food colours to the testing laboratories it was felt necessary to have reference food colour boxes. Such a measure, the technical committee felt, would ensure obtaining of uniform results of analysis and their proper interpretation. It is expected that this standard would facilitate fabrication of the reference food colour boxes.

1. SCOPE
1.1 '}'his standard prescribes requirements for reference food colour boxes.

2. RE~UIREMENTS 2.1 General- 'The reference food colour box shall contain a 20 g sample each of the food colours permitted under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955. The samples of food colours in all the boxes prepared at one time shall, as far as possible, be from a single batch of manufacture. 2.2 The box shall be made of plastic or from well seasoned wood. Each box shall have provision for keeping not less than twelve samples of reference food colour bottles. 2.3 The hottles shall be made of good quality amber glass or of opaque plastic and shall have well fitted cap made of plastic or any other suitable material. Capacity of each bottle shall be 40 g. In addition to the food colour, the bottle may contain 20 g of coloured silica gel in cheese cloth. 2.4 Colours - The samples of food colours contained in the bottles shall conform to the following Indian Standard specifications: IS: 1694-1974 'I'artrazine, food grade (first revision ) IS: 1695-1974 Sunset yellow, FCF, food grade (first recision )
�Method of Test for total dye content in food colour preparation��

S. MARKING
3.1 Each colour bottle shall bear a label ~iyjn~ the common name of the food colour and batch or code number. The folloYling information relating to each of the food colours shall be given on a card: a) Common name of the colour, b) Chemical name of the colour, c) Colour index number ( 195G), (1) Structural formula, e) Total analytical data of the' CO)OIlI\ and f) Batch or ('ocJ~ numhor, 3.2 Each colour box shall be marked with lh~ follo\ving: a) The words "Reference Food Colour Box " and b) Name and address of the manufaeturr-r,

3.3 DIS CertiOcation Marking
The product may also be marked with Standard Mark.
3.3.1 The use of tbe Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and tbe Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details of conditions under which the licence for the use of Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from tbe Bureau of Indian Standards.
